svg.title: Flush-control: one bucket shared by file writers
svg.desc: After initialization and the boot gate, control replaces the shared token budget under a mutex and broadcasts on its condition variable. Ordinary writers account pages after successful OS writes, release the mutex while waiting, and recheck on return. Log critical section owners and no-compensation modes bypass shortage waiting or accounting.
svg.text: Flush-control: one bucket shared by file writers
Verified mechanism at CUBRID f799e05; schematic, not a runtime snapshot.
1. Control task: after the boot gate opens
First accepted execution records time only.
Later: elapsed time + fixed/adaptive policy
Adaptive reads dirty-pressure feedback.
2. One shared TOKEN_BUCKET
fc_Token_bucket points to the bucket.
tokens / token_consumed
token_mutex + waiter_cond
Participating ordinary writers
A successful default-mode OS write comes first.
Then request one token per I/O page.
Bypass: FILEIO_WRITE_NO_COMPENSATE_WRITE
DWB staging/home use that bypass at f799e05.
3. Consume under token_mutex
Enough credit: consume and proceed.
Shortage: consume available credit, then wait.
Condition wait releases the mutex while sleeping.
LOG_CS_OWN: no shortage wait.
4. Control: replace, then broadcast
tokens = gen_tokens (not addition)
Waiters compete for the same renewed balance.
The first condition wait has no timeout.
5. Awakened writers recheck
Reacquire token_mutex; inspect the balance.
A broadcast does not reserve credit.
Returned waits count toward the retry cap.
Different from BCB completion and allocator queues
These waiters use the POSIX condition-variable mechanism, not next_wait_thrd.
Post-write pacing does not guarantee physical I/O rate, durable storage or bounded waiting.
Arrows show access or control flow; shared metadata still requires its own protection.
